job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan sat at his desk, staring at his math textbook. With the board exams approaching, he felt a tight knot in his stomach. He worried that if he didn't score perfectly, he would be a failure. His friend, Anjali, noticed him looking pale and asked if he was feeling overwhelmed. Rohan hesitated, fearing that talking about his stress might make him seem weak or 'mad'. Anjali smiled kindly and reminded him that mental health is a spectrum we all experience, not just the absence of illness. She explained that stress is a natural reaction, and some level of it actually helps us focus, though too much can be harmful. When Rohan confessed he felt hopeless, Anjali didn't panic. She told him that asking directly about feelings doesn't plant harmful ideas, but rather provides relief. She encouraged him to speak to a school counsellor, explaining that seeking professional help is a sign of strength, not just for those in a crisis. Anjali also reminded him that if a friend ever shares thoughts of self-harm, keeping it a secret is dangerous; one must inform a trusted adult immediately. Rohan felt a weight lift. He realized that his worth isn't defined by his marks, and taking short breaks to rest is actually essential for his brain to function well during the exam season.

items.evidence: She explained that stress is a natural reaction, and some level of it actually helps us focus, though too much can be harmful.
items.q: Meera feels a little stress before her test. What does Anjali's idea suggest about this?
options: A small amount can help her focus
Even a small amount will harm her
The more she feels, the better she scores
It shows she has a mental illness
items.explain: Stress is natural; some of it helps us focus, and only too much is harmful.

wrong.why: thinks more pressure always means better marks
thinks feeling nervous means mental illness

items.evidence: She encouraged him to speak to a school counsellor, explaining that seeking professional help is a sign of strength, not just for those in a crisis.
items.q: Rohan is not in a crisis. Should he still meet the school counsellor?
options: Yes, asking for help shows strength
No, that help is only for a crisis
No, asking for help shows he is weak
Yes, because he must be mentally ill
items.explain: Seeking professional help is a sign of strength, and it is not only for people in crisis.

wrong.why: thinks counselling is only for emergencies
thinks needing help is a weakness
mixes up mental health care with mental illness

items.evidence: She told him that asking directly about feelings doesn't plant harmful ideas, but rather provides relief.
items.q: Anjali asks a sad friend directly how he feels. What is the likely effect?
options: He feels lighter after sharing
He gets harmful new ideas from it
He feels weak for showing feelings
He feels worse since sadness is bad
items.explain: Asking directly about feelings does not plant harmful ideas; it gives the person relief.

wrong.why: believes the myth the passage rejects
thinks boys showing feelings is weakness

items.evidence: Anjali also reminded him that if a friend ever shares thoughts of self-harm, keeping it a secret is dangerous; one must inform a trusted adult immediately.
items.q: A friend shares thoughts of self-harm and begs you to stay quiet. What should you do?
options: Tell a trusted adult right away
Keep the promise and say nothing
Wait a few days to see if it passes
Tell them to try harder to cheer up
items.explain: Keeping self-harm thoughts secret is dangerous; you must tell a trusted adult immediately.

wrong.why: thinks worries are best kept hidden
thinks nothing can be done to help
thinks distress stops by trying harder

items.evidence: He realized that his worth isn't defined by his marks, and taking short breaks to rest is actually essential for his brain to function well during the exam season.
items.q: During exams, Rohan takes short rest breaks. How does this affect his studying?
options: It helps his brain work well
It wastes time he needs for study
It lowers the pressure he needs to succeed
It shows he is not trying hard enough
items.explain: Short breaks to rest are essential for the brain to function well during exams.

thinks more pressure gives better results
